title: Riemann–Roch and coherent Serre duality
statement:
Fix a smooth projective geometrically connected curve $C/k$, and set
$g=\dim_kH^1(C,\cO_C)$. (Smooth proper geometrically connected curves
over a field are projective (Stacks Project, Tag 0A26), so this includes
the proper curves of the main text.) For an invertible sheaf $\cL$ on $C$,

$$
\chi(C,\cL)=\deg\cL+1-g,
\qquad
H^1(C,\cL)^\vee\simeq H^0(C,\omega_{C/k}\otimes\cL^{-1}),
\qquad \deg\omega_{C/k}=2g-2.
$$

These identifications commute with field extension. In particular, if
$\deg\cL>2g-2$, then

$$
H^1(C,\cL)=0,
\qquad h^0(C,\cL)=\deg\cL+1-g.
$$

Here $\deg\cL=\deg D=\sum_xn_x[\kappa(x):k]$ for any divisor
$D=\sum_xn_x\,x$ with $\cL\cong\cO_C(D)$ (well defined, since principal
divisors have degree $0$), and $\chi(C,\cL)=h^0(C,\cL)-h^1(C,\cL)$.

*Complements* (also proved in this sketch and used in this block). The
Riemann–Roch formula extends to coherent $\cF$ as
$\chi(\cF)=\deg\cF+\operatorname{rk}(\cF)(1-g)$, with
$\deg\cF=\dim_kH^0(C,\mathcal T)+\deg\det(\cF/\mathcal T)$ for the torsion
subsheaf $\mathcal T$; and:

1. **(G)** *positive degree $\Rightarrow$ ample:* a line bundle $\cL$
on $C$ with $\deg\cL>0$ is ample;
1. **(H)** *affine complement:* if $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor
on a proper $k$-scheme $X$ with $\cO_X(D)$ ample, then
$X\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(D)$ is affine.

proof.text: Smooth projectivity supplies integrality, properness, Noetherianity and regularity; smoothness supplies geometric reducedness. Use the source GlobalSectionsBijective instance and the already proved Modules.eulerChar_eq_degree_add and eulerChar_eq_finrankH_zero_sub_finrankH_one for line-bundle RR and Euler normalization.

proof.text: Apply regular_curve_divisor_calculus for invertibility, O(0), tensor multiplication, principal divisors and the closed-point modification sequence. The quotient is finitely presented as a cokernel of invertible modules, hence coherent. Its given isomorphism with the residue-field skyscraper identifies its Euler characteristic with [kappa(x):k]: away from x every stalk vanishes, the support is at most a singleton, and evaluation of H0 on the top open is k-linearly equivalent to kappa(x). The scalar check is Hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap_apply. Use eulerChar_zero_dim_support and Euler additivity to compute degree O([x]). Tensor multiplication and degree_tensorObj make degree O(D) an additive homomorphism. Finsupp.addHom_ext and extensionality on the integer generator extend the equality to all integral divisors. Transport along O(D) isomorphisms. The principal-divisor isomorphism and degree_unit then give weighted degree zero.

Transport degree_pullback and eulerChar_pullback through picardRRPullbackIso. Compose H.baseChange_bijective_of_isSeparated with H.mapLinearEquiv for bijectivity of the canonical map. Specialize the module-cohomology trace equation to the identity on omega and scalars c=d=1. blueprint_update.statement:
Fix a smooth proper curve $C/k$ with $H^0(C,\cO_C)=k$, and set
$g=\dim_kH^1(C,\cO_C)$. (For smooth proper $C$, the condition
$H^0(C,\cO_C)=k$ is equivalent to geometric connectedness, and such curves
are projective (Stacks Project, Tag 0A26).) For an invertible sheaf $\cL$ on $C$,

$$
\chi(C,\cL)=\deg\cL+1-g,
\qquad
H^1(C,\cL)^\vee\simeq H^0(C,\omega_{C/k}\otimes\cL^{-1}),
\qquad \deg\omega_{C/k}=2g-2.
$$

In particular, if
$\deg\cL>2g-2$, then

$$
H^1(C,\cL)=0,
\qquad h^0(C,\cL)=\deg\cL+1-g.
$$

The genus and the degree are invariant under extension of the ground
field.

Here $\deg\cL=\deg D=\sum_xn_x[\kappa(x):k]$ for any divisor
$D=\sum_xn_x\,x$ with $\cL\cong\cO_C(D)$ (well defined, since principal
divisors have degree $0$), and $\chi(C,\cL)=h^0(C,\cL)-h^1(C,\cL)$.

*Complements* (also proved in this sketch and used in this block). The
Riemann–Roch formula extends to coherent $\cF$ as
$\chi(\cF)=\deg\cF+\operatorname{rk}(\cF)(1-g)$, with
$\deg\cF=\dim_kH^0(C,\mathcal T)+\deg\det(\cF/\mathcal T)$ for the torsion
subsheaf $\mathcal T$; and:

1. **(G)** *positive degree $\Rightarrow$ ample:* a line bundle $\cL$
on $C$ with $\deg\cL>0$ is ample;
1. **(H)** *affine complement:* if $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor
on a proper $k$-scheme $X$ with $\cO_X(D)$ ample, then
$X\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(D)$ is affine.

proof.text:
This is coherent duality and Riemann–Roch for smooth curves (Stacks
Project, Tag 0B5B); the duality is given by the residue trace on
differentials ([det-thm-picard-duality], with $n=1$, $q=1$, $\cF=\cL$).

*Riemann–Roch.* By additivity of $\chi$ in short exact sequences, the
torsion part of a coherent $\cF$ (for which $\chi=h^0$ is the length,
i.e. the degree) and a filtration of the locally free quotient by line
bundles (along which $\deg\det$ is additive) reduce the formula to line
bundles $\cO_C(D)$. There
$0\to\cO_C(D-x)\to\cO_C(D)\to\kappa(x)\to0$ gives
$\chi(\cO_C(D))=\chi(\cO_C(D-x))+[\kappa(x):k]$ (coherent cohomology
vanishes in degrees $\ge2$ on the one-dimensional noetherian space $C$,
so $\chi=h^0-h^1$ throughout); applied to $D$ when $n_x>0$ and to $D+x$
when $n_x<0$, it lowers $\sum_x|n_x|$ by one and leaves $\chi-\deg$
unchanged, so by induction $\chi(\cO_C(D))=\deg D+\chi(\cO_C)$, and
$\chi(\cO_C)=h^0-h^1=1-g$ because $H^0(C,\cO_C)=k$. (In particular
$C$ is connected, and, its local rings being regular, integral.)

*Canonical degree.* Duality with $\cL=\cO_C$ gives $h^0(\omega_{C/k})=g$
and $h^1(\omega_{C/k})=h^0(\cO_C)=1$, so
$\deg\omega_{C/k}=\chi(\omega_{C/k})-\chi(\cO_C)=(g-1)-(1-g)=2g-2$.

*Field extension.* For $K/k$, flat base change identifies
$H^i(C_K,\cL_K)=H^i(C,\cL)\otimes_kK$ for all $i$, so
$\chi(C_K,\cL_K)=\chi(C,\cL)$; applied to $\cL$ and to $\cO_C$ this shows
that the degree $\chi(\cL)-\chi(\cO_C)$ and the genus $h^1(\cO_C)$ are
preserved, and that $H^0(C_K,\cO_{C_K})=K$, so $C_K$ again satisfies the
hypotheses.

*Vanishing.* If $\deg\cL>2g-2$, the dual sheaf
$\omega_{C/k}\otimes\cL^{-1}$ has negative degree. A nonzero section of
an invertible sheaf on an integral curve has an effective zero divisor,
of degree $\ge0$, so a negative-degree sheaf has no nonzero section.
Hence $H^1(C,\cL)=0$, and Riemann–Roch gives
$h^0(C,\cL)=\chi(C,\cL)=\deg\cL+1-g$.

*(G).* Ampleness descends along $\Spec\bar k\to\Spec k$ and degree is
preserved by flat base change, so we may take $k$ algebraically closed,
where every closed point is rational. For $m\deg\cL\ge2g+1$ and closed
points $P,Q$ (possibly equal), the range $\deg>2g-2$ above gives
$h^0(\cL^{\otimes m}(-P))=h^0(\cL^{\otimes m})-1$ and
$h^0(\cL^{\otimes m}(-P-Q))=h^0(\cL^{\otimes m})-2$, i.e.
$\cL^{\otimes m}$ is base-point free and separates points and tangent
vectors; hence $\cL^{\otimes m}$ is very ample and $\cL$ is ample.

*(H).* Classical: the complement of the support of an ample effective
Cartier divisor $D$ is the non-vanishing locus of the canonical section
of $\cO_X(D)$, and non-vanishing loci of sections of an ample sheaf on a
proper scheme are affine.
